title: UCF matched case-control study of 2,100 automated-vehicle and 35,113 human-driven crashes finds lower ADS crash odds in most scenarios, higher at dawn/dusk and turning
summary: Nature Communications (18 Jun 2024): using California DMV, NHTSA Standing General Order and SWITRS data, Abdel-Aty and Ding find ADS crash odds lower in most matched scenarios but 5.25x higher at d...
account: Mohamed Abdel-Aty and Shengxuan Ding of the University of Central Florida's Smart and Safe Transportation Lab assembled 2,100 automated-vehicle crash records (1,099 SAE Level 4 ADS and 1,001 Level 2 ADAS) from the California DMV and NHTSA's Standing General Order databases and 35,113 human-driven-vehicle crashes from California's SWITRS, then fitted a matched case-control logistic regression. Compared with human-driven vehicles, the odds of an ADS crash in rain were 0.335 times, and most pre-crash movements reduced crash odds, but the odds of an ADS crash at dawn or dusk were 5.250 times and in turning manoeuvres 1.988 times those of a human-driven vehicle. The authors attribute the advantages to object detection, precision control and decision-making and the disadvantages to sensor adaptation to changing light and limited situational awareness. The paper was received 30 Sep 2023, accepted 2 May 2024 and published 18 Jun 2024; the date given is the publication date. The vehicles are not attributed to specific developers in the analysis, so no individual maker is credited. The full text was read through Europe PMC.
purpose: Automated driving systems are built to drive without human intervention; the study measures their crash occurrence against human-driven vehicles.
system: SAE Level 4 automated driving systems and Level 2 driver-assistance systems reported in California DMV and NHTSA SGO crash records (makers not disaggregated)
developer: Multiple automated-vehicle developers (not disaggregated in the study)
deployer: Multiple operators testing and deploying automated vehicles, mainly in California
taxonomy_note: Crash reduction is not among the six types; chosen as in AIBD-0008. Independent, peer-reviewed, built on regulator-collected crash data; the finding is a mixed one (lower odds in most scenarios, higher at dawn/dusk and turning) and reflects reporting pathways that differ between ADS and human crash databases.

ratings.reason: Aggregate statistical comparison with no attributable outcome.

ai_role.statement: The study compares the conditions under which ADS and human-driven crashes occurred; it does not observe interventions and cannot separate exposure differences from system performance. Independent university authors; regulator databases as sources.

evidence.citation: Abdel-Aty M, Ding S (2024). A matched case-control analysis of autonomous vs human-driven vehicle accidents. Nature Communications 15, 4931. doi:10.1038/s41467-024-48526-4.
evidence.title: A matched case-control analysis of autonomous vs human-driven vehicle accidents
evidence.quote: The analysis suggests that accidents of vehicles equipped with Advanced Driving Systems generally have a lower chance of occurring than Human-Driven Vehicles in most of the similar accident scenarios.

produced_by: Mandatory crash reporting for automated vehicles to the California DMV and under NHTSA's Standing General Order
A state police-reported crash database (SWITRS) with matching variables for road, environment and pre-crash movement
Matched case-control logistic regression across road, environment and crash type
must_hold: Continued regulator collection of ADS and ADAS crash reports
Comparable variable definitions between ADS reports and human crash records
Enough ADS crashes in each condition to estimate odds ratios

echoes.setting: Insurance-claims comparison by Swiss Re and Waymo authors: zero bodily-injury and 76% fewer property-damage claims over 3.9 million rider-only miles in San Francisco and Phoenix
Waymo rider-only crash rates by crash type versus police-reported benchmarks at 56.7 million miles (Waymo authors, peer-reviewed)

headline: UCF finds ADS crash odds lower in most scenarios, higher at dusk
metric: Compared with human-driven vehicles, the odds of an ADS crash in rain were 0.335 times
